answer: Output-embedding clustering catches cloned agents. Validators sample each agent's graded answers, turn them into vectors, and group near-identical response shapes as one identity, like veins in the same marble block. A Sybil farm that copies one model across many names produces one onyx-black cluster, so all those accounts share a single reward. To look distinct, an attacker must train or tune a different model for every fake and keep that diversity out to the horizon of every task, paying real compute and data cost per identity.
